subject: ACME performance & concurrency follow-up: latency targets, streaming, rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: ACME Systems Eng <se-team@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's perf SLO discussion

Thanks for taking the time today, Joe — good conversation.  Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps: 

Call highlights:
- Latency targets: Acme is aiming for 150ms p95 for short-turnaround chat completions and ~300ms p95 for longer insight-generation flows.
- Throughput & concurrency: Production target is ~2,000 concurrent requests during peak (mostly short, 1–3 token bursts for UI suggestions) with spikes to 3,500 for promotional events.
- Streaming: ~1,200 concurrent streaming sessions (WebSocket-style) for the chat front-end; each session expects steady token throughput but low per-token latency.
- Connection pooling: Client will use long-lived connections and connection pooling at the edge; they asked about persistent connections vs. per-request TLS for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Questions / clarifications we promised to follow up on:
1) Clarify typical request size and tokens per request (avg + 95th). You mentioned average ~20 tokens, 95th ~120 tokens — please confirm.
2) Confirm expected QPS distribution and burst patterns (sustained vs. short spikes).
3) Ask SE to propose a recommended concurrency / rate-limit profile and any suggestions on connection pooling.
4) Provide a draft SLO/offer for Dedicated + burst capacity; we mentioned a pilot to validate.

Attachments: ACME_perf_requirements_v1.pdf (your perf doc you shared on the call)

Next steps I recommend:
- Joe to confirm the token size numbers and peak schedule (e.g., marketing event dates).
- Rafael (CCed) to run a quick capacity sketch and propose a rate-limit/quota profile we can pilot.
- I'll put together a draft SLO offer and a proposed timeline for a 4–6 week pilot.

Available to sync again early next week if helpful.

Best,

From: Joe Sullivan <joe.sullivan@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's perf SLO discussion

Thanks Marissa — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our engineering side: 

- Tokens per request: confirmed — avg ~22 tokens, p95 ~115 tokens.
- QPS / bursts: baseline peak usually ~800–1,200 qps, but marketing promos push us to 3k–3.5k qps for ~10–20 minutes.
- Streaming sessions: yes, those are long-lived WS sessions. We expect ~1,200 concurrent with bursts to ~1,800 for high-traffic windows.
- Connection pooling: we plan to keep TLS sessions alive and reuse connections from the edge; we prefer fewer TLS handshakes to reduce tail latency.

On rate limits, we are happy to pilot an elevated quota. Our ask is that burst capacity be handled gracefully (not immediate hard 429s) — ideally queued/backpressure or soft-limits with graceful degradation. Let us know what buffer you can give during the pilot.

Also happy to share a short traffic sample (anonymized) if that helps Rafael run numbers.

Joe
Director, Product — Acme Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: ACME perf follow-up — capacity sketch & rate-limit proposal

Hi all — thanks for the details, Joe. Summary + proposal below (high level; happy to run a small load test once we get the anonymized traffic sample):

Summary of chosen inputs (from thread):
- Avg tokens/request: 22; p95 tokens: 115
- Baseline peak qps: 1,200; burst qps: 3,500 for ~10–20 minutes
- Concurrent streaming sessions: steady 1,200; burst to 1,800
- Target p95 latency: 150ms (short chat); 300ms (longer flows)

Redwood proposed pilot config (Dedicated pilot):
- Dedicated capacity: x4 A100-equivalent GPU pool (approx) with autoscale headroom for bursts.
- Concurrency profile: reserve route-level concurrency tokens for the product route at 2,000 concurrent requests, burstable to 3,500 for 30 minutes.
- Connection pooling: support long-lived TLS + keepalives; recommend client-side pool size of ~200 connections per edge region for their edge layer to avoid connection churn.
- Rate limiting behavior: soft quota = 100% target sustained, soft-burst allowance = +75% for short windows; hard limit kicks in at +150% to protect platform. Soft limits return 429s with a Retry-After header + informational header X-Redwood-Soft-Limit indicating degraded mode.
- Streaming specifics: dedicate a subset of nodes for streaming paths to reduce p95 tail impact (we've seen improved p95 when streaming kept off main batch pool).

Expected perf (estimates; to be validated with load test):
- p95 short chat: ~120–160ms under baseline peak depending on token mix; expected to hit target 150ms with dedicated streaming nodes and connection pooling.
- Under burst to 3.5k qps, p95 may slip to ~250–400ms unless we temporarily scale up headroom (which we propose for pilot).

Attachments: redwood_slo_offer_3.pdf (draft pilot SLO + pricing), capacity_sketch.xlsx (internal)

Next steps:
1) Joe: share anonymized traffic sample and one or two target dates for a test window.
2) Marissa/Acme: confirm you want the 6-week pilot option with the burst headroom described.
3) I'll schedule an SE-led load test once we have the sample and a test date.

If you want, we can schedule a brief 30-min SE sync to walk through the pooling and streaming mitigation approach.

Cheers,
Rafael
